messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=redwood-autoscaler | alert=INFERENCE_QUEUE_BACKLOG_HIGH | severity=page
pagerduty-bot: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/P12345678 — page routed to alice (oncall)
alice (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Checking region-us-west metrics and autoscaler logs.
sam: Noted impact: increased 5xx retries from customers behind streaming endpoints? Any customer-facing pages yet?
maya: No PD from customers, but frontend 429s rising for a few customers on us-west-2.
incident-bot: Grafana dashboards: http://grafana/redwood/d/autoscale/queue-backlog?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2 — queue depth spiking for inference-queue (~1200 -> 4800 in 6m)
leo: Autoscaler events look like scaling actions queued but not provisioning new pods. K8s shows NodePool quota throttle: "InsufficientQuota: can't provision more".
alice (oncall): Running quick checks. `kubectl get hpa -n inference` -> HPA CPU utilization ~45%, target 60% (so CPU-based HPA not triggering). Queue-based scaler should've fired.
irene: Confirming: our KEDA-based scaler uses custom metric from queue length. Alerts show scaler received metric but scale down lockouts present? Trying `kubectl describe scaledobject inference-queue-scaled`.
sam: If HPA isn't the driver, maybe the autoscaler is blocked at cloud provider
ops-runner: I'm seeing API errors from cloud provider: rateLimitedCreateInstances; recent quota event 429 on ASG requests.
alice (oncall): Ok that matches. We have two failure modes: provider quota preventing new nodes OR preemptible/spot exhaustion causing provisioning fallback to backoff. Which one is it?
incident-bot: Cloud control-plane: 6x createInstance failures in last 4m for pool-inference-usw2 (quota limit). See cloud-console link: https://cloud/console/quotas#pool-inference-usw2
maya: Customer impact: a handful of API calls experiencing >2s latency, and some streaming sessions failing with retries. Listing top impacted customers: AcmeCorp, FathomAI, EchoSearch.
leo: Quick mitigation: we can temporarily route new traffic to us-east while we spin up capacity here. Need a fast rollout of routing rule.
alice (oncall): Actions: 1) throttle non-critical background jobs to reduce queue pressure 2) attempt manual node pool increase via cloud console (if quota allows) 3) route traffic away as fallback. I'm executing 1 now.
alice (oncall): Throttling background ingestion queues: `kubectl scale deployment ingestion-worker --replicas=0 --namespace=batch` (temporary)
ops-runner: Throttles applied. Background queue consumption dropped ~30% in 90s.
sam: Trying manual node create: `gcloud compute instances create --zone=us-west2-a --num-nodes=4 --labels=pool=inference` -> got 403 Quota exceeded.
irene: I can request an emergency quota bump but it'll take ~20-30min. Request submitted to cloud support with priority=emergency.
pagerduty-bot: Escalation timer: 8m until escalation to L2 if not acknowledged (current: L1=alice)
maya: While quota is being escalated, let's enable routing to us-east for new sessions. How safe is cross-region routing for these customers? We have session affinity concerns.
leo: For non-stateful streaming we can route. For affinity-bound sessions, we should only route new sessions. We'll add header-based routing: `x-redwood-prefer-region: us-east-1` for new token issues.
alice (oncall): Rolling out routing change to API gateway: `kubectl apply -f gateway/route-temp-us-east.yaml` — patching now.
incident-bot: Deploybot: change in gateway 'route-temp-us-east' started by alice (oncall). CI checks passed. Deploying.
ops-runner: Gateway rollout OK on 3/3 nodes. New session traffic now observed to be 60% -> us-east in the last minute.
sam: That reduced queue growth rate by ~45% — good.
leo: Next: if quota bump delayed, fallback is to enable autoscaler to scale pods (not nodes) with more aggressive pre-warming (but we may starve existing pods). Risky.
irene: Another quick hack: enable model-quantization fallback for low-priority customers to reduce per-token CPU and allow more requests to be served per pod. We can flip a feature-flag for <trial> customers.
maya: Let's only enable quantization fallback for background/low-priority (non-paying trial) customers. Confirmed with product.
alice (oncall): Agreed. Enabling quantization fallback for non-pay tiers: `curl -X POST https://config-api/flags -d '{"quant_fallback": "nonpay"}'` (dry-run then apply).
incident-bot: Config change requested by alice (oncall). Running dry-run... dry-run OK. Applying now.
ops-runner: Quantization fallback applied. Observed per-pod token throughput +25% in 2m.
sam: Good. Combined with routing and throttle, queue length peaked and now trending down (4800 -> 1600 over 7m).
pagerduty-bot: Reminder: if incident not resolved in 15m, escalate to engineering-sre rotation.
alice (oncall): Cloud support responded: quota increase scheduled in 12 minutes. They gave soft limit until we finish migration.
irene: I'll follow up to confirm once the nodes are provisioned. Also creating a post-incident ticket to review quota monitoring and automated emergency bump flow.
maya: Customer comms: drafting a temporary status update for affected customers indicating degraded performance in us-west and mitigation moving traffic to us-east. Will share draft here.
alice (oncall): Handing off - I need to jump to another page. Maya — you are primary. Sam and Leo remain on standby for infra actions. Irene please track post-incident actions.
maya: Taking over. Summary: routing change applied, background jobs throttled, quant-fallback enabled for non-pay tiers, cloud support queueed quota bump. Monitoring for stabilization.
leo: On standby to run manual node provisioning once quota confirmed, or revert routing if problems.
sam: Also tracking the KEDA scaler logs to ensure it doesn't re-enable aggressive downscale later and stomp pods. Will set temporary annotations to prevent scale-to-zero.
ops-runner: Noted. I'll keep an eye on endpoint error rates and will open a PD incident if customer-impact resumes.
maya: Draft status update (copied): "We are currently mitigating increased inference queue backlog in us-west. We have temporarily routed new requests to us-east, throttled background jobs, and applied a temporary model fallback to increase throughput for lower-priority workloads. Core services are processing backlog and we expect restoration within 30-45 minutes. Engineers are working with cloud provider on quota increase to restore capacity in us-west." Comments?
alice (oncall): looks good, add mention that customer sessions already in progress may be affected, only new sessions routed.
maya: Updated. Posting to status.redwood.com now.
incident-bot: Status update posted by maya. link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-202305
sam: Queue depth now ~900 and still falling. 5xx error rate reduced back to baseline for paying customers.
irene: Created follow-up ticket: TICKET-9482 — review autoscaler-to-quota runbook, add automated preemptive quota checks for node pools.
maya: I'm going to keep watch for 30m and then close the thread if steady. Thanks all for fast responses :heart:
alice (oncall): Thanks team. Reopening if anything spikes.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: alert cleared for INFERENCE_QUEUE_BACKLOG_HIGH. Closing thread.
